Title: May 21, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Meeting - Regular Meeting

Topic1.Title: Open Comment: San Lazaro Mobile Home Park Residents Seeking Support for Resident Purchase
Topic1.Summary: Multiple San Lazaro residents, including Marcus Christopher, Elizabeth Hieronymus, John Bellos, David Ulrick, and Amela Alkanovic, spoke about threats of displacement if the park is sold to an outside investor. They described the community's importance to workers, students, and families, and asked the city for financial and political support to help residents purchase the park for $42.5 million. Council members and staff expressed support, noting the city and county are commissioning a new appraisal and exploring possible funding mechanisms.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment: Golden West Senior Housing Utility and Parking Changes
Topic2.Summary: Residents including Patty Hayward, Kathy Arp, and E.J. Geroux raised concerns that Golden West will end bundled cable, television, and telephone services as of September 1 and begin charging for parking. Residents on fixed incomes worried about the cost increase. Housing staff explained that a Comcast contract is expiring, that free Wi-Fi will continue with a rent reduction of about $40 to $45 per month, and that Boulder Housing Partners will provide support for transitions.

Topic3.Title: Open Comment: Municipal Airport Local Control and FAA Grants
Topic3.Summary: Several speakers, including Jeff Calhoun, Daniel Howard, Matthew Bible, Hep Ingham, and Laura Kaplan, urged the council to pursue local control of the airport and avoid FAA grant obligations. Speakers cited noise, leaded fuel, and enforcement concerns, and referenced airports in Santa Monica and Torrance that operate with local restrictions. Kaplan asked for a redo of the recent study session, arguing that it contained incomplete information. Staff responded that funding decisions and FAA control of airspace are complex and that the topic will return to council.

Topic4.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic4.Summary: Council considered items 3A and 3B on the consent agenda. Council Member Wallach asked to note a no vote on item 3B, an ordinance amending Title 7 height limitations, citing concerns about imprecise drafting. The consent agenda was otherwise approved unanimously.

Topic5.Title: Call-Up Check-Ins
Topic5.Summary: Council reviewed item 4A, a site review for redevelopment of 777 Broadway with 63 residential units, and item 4B, a Landmarks Board decision not to designate 990 Arapahoe Avenue as an individual landmark. No council members called up either item. Council Member Matt raised concerns about the landmarking process and suggested reviewing it at next year's retreat.

Topic6.Title: Public Hearing: Ordinance 8750, Adjustment to Base Budget One
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented the first adjustment to base for the 2026 fiscal year, totaling $18.6 million, including $13.1 million from fund balance, $5.3 million in mid-year grants, and $129,000 in additional revenue. Major items included radio replacement funding, affordable housing project carryovers, and wildfire mitigation grants. Council discussed radio replacement timing, fund balance sources, and community engagement staffing, and a speaker criticized communications spending. Council unanimously adopted the ordinance.

Topic7.Title: Matters from the Mayor and Council: Criteria for Straw Polls and Reconsideration
Topic7.Summary: City Attorney Teresa Taylor Tate explained that study sessions provide non-binding direction to staff, that straw polls are not addressed in council procedure but can indicate consensus, and that reconsideration applies only to formal council actions after a material change in law or fact. Council discussed how to frame straw polls, whether study sessions may include informational items, and how to avoid confusion with formal votes. Council agreed to rename straw polls as a 'non-binding nod of five' and to codify the use of study sessions for informational items. Staff will also provide a summary of upcoming Council Action Calendar items.
